Use layers for decorative divider lines (gradient or fill strokes)

entries.feels_like: Applies visual effects to sections and elements — glass (frosted glass with physics-based refraction), drop shadow, inner shadow, glow, opacity, blur, backdrop blur, brightness, contrast, saturation, grayscale, and sepia. entries.feels_like: Positions a section fixed relative to the viewport, removing it from the normal document flow. Configure the fixed edge (top, bottom, left, right) and offset from that edge. entries.feels_like: A section that wraps a form — an ordered list of field blocks (text, email, textarea, select, checkbox) posted to an API route. Handles method, action URL, and static payload values. Use for contact forms, newsletter sign-ups, and survey blocks.

the interaction is a range slider (use element.range)

entries.feels_like: Applies a parallax scroll speed multiplier to a section — elements inside move at a different rate than the page scroll, creating depth. you need sticky positioning (use section.sticky)
you need entrance animations on scroll (use motionTiming.entrancePreset)

known_limitations: scrollSpeed is a multiplier — 0 means the section stays fixed relative to viewport
initialX and initialY set the starting translate offset in pixels or CSS units
Parallax effects stack with entrance animations — order matters for perceived depth

entries.feels_like: Enables drag-and-drop reordering of child elements within a content block section. Configure the reorder axis (x or y), drag unit (frame or content), and drag behavior (elastic snap, free, or none). you need free-form element dragging (use motion.drag)
you need a static ordered list (use section.contentBlock without reorder)

reorderDragUnit: 'content' drags the visual element; 'frame' uses a drag handle overlay
reorderAxis must match the content block's flexDirection — x for row, y for column

entries.feels_like: An expandable/collapsible section with two element states — collapsed and revealed. Expands on hover, click, external trigger, or button press, animating the container from collapsedSize to expandedSize with staggered child reveal. Tab-strip selector switching between multiple views

collapsedElements are shown only when collapsed; revealedElements shown only when revealed

proposal_hints.new_variant_value: N/A — no variant field on section.reveal

entries.feels_like: A scrollable section whose scroll position drives a named progress trigger — horizontal, vertical, or both axes. does_not_cover.what: Snapping carousel with per-item scale and opacity

entries.feels_like: Maps the section's vertical scroll position through the viewport to its opacity. Define an input range (scroll progress 0→1) and an output range (opacity values), and the section's opacity interpolates smoothly between them. Use for fade-in hero reveals, fade-out footers, or any section whose visibility should track scroll position. Works on any section type.
not_this_if: you need scroll-progress-driven action triggers (use section.scrollContainer)
you need entrance/exit animations (use motionTiming.entrancePreset / exitPreset)
you need a fixed or sticky section that tracks scroll (use section.sticky / section.fixed)

entries.feels_like: Makes a section stick to the top or bottom of the viewport while the user scrolls past it. Configure the stick edge, offset from the edge, and responsive positioning. entries.feels_like: An invisible intersection-observer sentinel. entries.feels_like: Conditionally shows or hides a section based on page-builder variable values. Define single or compound conditions with operators (equals, notEquals, gt, gte, lt, lte, contains, startsWith) and AND/OR logic. Use for feature flags, A/B test variants, user-state-driven visibility, or any content gating that depends on variable state. Works on any section type.

you need an animated expand/collapse (use section.reveal)

Wire `cursorTriggers` on a section to drive parallax effects, spotlight positions, or variable bindings that follow the cursor.

throttleMs defaults are implementation-defined; set explicitly for predictable fps
Cursor position is relative to the viewport, not the section

shortcuts are active only while the section is mounted

Wire `action` on element.button, or wire `onClick` on any section or element via triggerActionSchema. The primary interaction trigger for modals, reveals, player commands, and variable mutations.

you need a keyboard shortcut (use trigger.keyboard)
the click is navigation — a link (use element.link or element.button with href)

Click on a button inside a section also bubbles — avoid double-wiring

you need continuous scroll progress (use trigger.onProgress)

you only need a fire-once event on entry (use trigger.onVisible)
